Physical Orin first boot, audits 49fa7f963 and 2805

This is a supplement to the existing full Orin seed host-writer rehearsal and
orin-wpa3-rehearsal.py. Reuse their release verification, exact radio/AP identity
and recovery records. The host-writer test does not boot hardware. The WPA3
procedure starts with an operational board. This supplement observes the missing
transition from a newly written image to persistent name, Wi-Fi and enrollment.
All cases start not_run. Generation performs only local file reads and hashing.

Prepare one exact reserved target

1. Reserve board serial @SERIAL@ with its named owner. This plan covers a genuine
   NVIDIA developer kit and its selected NVMe/eMMC storage, not a custom carrier.
   Record module/carrier model and revisions, module serial, recovery ECID, USB
   physical path, storage model/serial/capacity, Wi-Fi chipset/firmware/driver,
   station MAC and power arrangement. Keep serial console and independent direct
   Ethernet/USB management. The management link must have NO Internet forwarding,
   bridging, DNS proxy or connection sharing for the delayed-network case. The
   tested radio must be the only egress path. Record routes and both host/board
   link configuration to prove that condition. Do not change a shared router.

2. Use the public release descriptor and locally verified full archive from the
   existing Orin seed procedure, or acquire the exact board/storage release from
   the official device manifest. Record its immutable URL, version, size and SHA.
   The generator verifies those local bytes. It does not install that local archive
   by fiat: run the generated plan and require its artifact_url, artifact_sha256,
   device_type, storage and version to match the descriptor. A generation query in
   the descriptor is acceptable only if the URL without that query and the full
   digest match. Reject a moving latest alias or mismatched release. Keep plan JSON,
   signed/published producer provenance, full CLI SHA/revision and Agent SHA/revision.
   Verify source revisions include the relevant changes. Do not infer code from a
   version string. Record the image's boot scripts and Agent selection separately.

3. Review recovery_record with the owner before any flash. Include actual recovery
   button/cable/power sequence for this board, previous image/storage backup and
   restore plan, independent console access, AP rollback, and Cloud test-device
   cleanup owner. No device is erased by generating a plan. At each physical write,
   present the newly observed exact target fingerprint and erase scope and obtain
   that owner's authorization. Old authorization for another device or an earlier
   fingerprint is insufficient. Do not pass --force or bypass internal disk checks.
   Use the CLI's returned physical instructions and elevation flow. Never guess a
   /dev path. Flash failure remains a failure; do not turn it into a blind retry.

4. Use a dedicated lab SSID @SSID@, predeclared BSSID and isolated credentials.
   Record AP model/firmware/security/channel, DHCP lease and association logging,
   station MAC policy, and the owner-approved method to delay only this SSID.
   Reserve the unique device name @NAME@ in the intended lab tenant before the
   enrollment case. Verify the exact logged-in Cloud host/tenant/account; do not
   reuse an unrelated enrolled device identity. Public protocol observations and
   sensitive credentials have separate evidence storage. Do not publish passphrases,
   EABs, account/device private keys or raw provisioning/config files. No terminal
   transcript should record password entry.

Case A: jobs CLI seed applied by the first real boot (49fa7f963)

5. In a private local terminal run start-seeded-job.py. It prompts for the lab
   password and calls the exact generated jobs start prefix with --wifi. The
   password is not saved in this plan or shell history. The current CLI accepts
   --wifi as an argument, so it is transiently visible in that local child process's
   argv. Use only reserved credentials on a trusted operator host. The helper
   refuses nonterminal input and exits after 60 seconds; it only plans a job.
   Record the returned job ID, device_name, Wi-Fi SSID, open_wifi and target plan.
   Require open_wifi to be empty and the intended name/SSID to be present. Save
   only redacted job JSON. The private input belongs to that exact job, is kept
   at most 24 hours and is single-attempt material. Do not read it into a shared log.

6. Follow that job's physical instructions and run, with the observed values:
     "$CLI" install jobs status --job-id "$JOB_ID"
     "$CLI" install jobs resume --job-id "$JOB_ID"
   The second command probes; inspect the returned target fingerprint, ECID/path,
   storage and erase scope against step1. Only after exact-target erase approval:
     "$CLI" install jobs resume --job-id "$JOB_ID" --target-id "$FINGERPRINT" --confirm-erase
   Record each state and full sanitized worker log through write completion.
   The jobs path does not support --binary or pre-enrollment. Record the actual
   downloaded arm64 Agent artifact selected by the worker and compare its SHA to
   the inventory. A changed release selection makes binary provenance incomplete;
   do not silently credit this run to the requested revision. Never add unsupported
   flags or replace the installed Agent after boot to make this first-boot test pass.
   Name/Wi-Fi injection, config release and write completion must all succeed.
   Retain a private hash of the exact job provisioning input and the worker's seed
   preparation evidence. If direct seed readback is available before boot through
   the returned recovery workflow, retain its private hash and redacted [device]/
   [wifi] values; do not mount a live target behind the installer's back. No secret
   readback is required to be uploaded. The real boot observations below are mandatory.

7. Start timestamped serial capture before the first power-on/recovery release.
   With the dedicated AP available, allow at most @SECONDS@ seconds for this first
   boot. Match physical serial/storage/boot ID to the fresh write. From the console
   record uname, /etc/os-release, the actual Agent unit/ExecStart/MainPID, and SHA256
   of /proc/PID/exe. Compare it with the recorded downloaded Agent and source pin.
   A config-seeded Agent may restart itself once; record both boot-time processes
   and the final durable executable, not just the image's initial Agent version.
   Require the journal to show name and Wi-Fi application from config, with no
   retained invalid/unreadable seed or profile registration failure. Successful
   profile registration alone is insufficient: require actual AP association.

8. Read the live profile UUID from nmcli's connection/device status, then run
   sh board-snapshot.sh "$OBSERVED_PROFILE_UUID" from the physical console,
   saving stdout/stderr and exit
   status on the operator host. Require /etc/wendyos/device-name == @NAME@,
   /etc/hostname and running hostname == wendyos-@NAME@. Record the selected live
   NetworkManager profile UUID, autoconnect, interface, SSID and nonsecret security
   fields, plus its persistent keyfile existence/permissions. Do not use nmcli
   --show-secrets. Require AP-confirmed BSSID/station, the expected DHCP address,
   live iw association and five gateway replies bound to the Wi-Fi interface.
   Ethernet cannot satisfy the bound ping. Preserve config consumption status;
   if wendy.conf remains, privately identify its remaining section and failure.
   A partly retained seed is not a complete first-boot application pass.

9. From the management host run discover and verify at the actual observed direct
   address. If DHCP changed the planned address, first corroborate serial console,
   station MAC and physical board identity, then use that explicit address. Require
   actual expected OS/type and name/mDNS advertisement, and save the returned public
   key. Run jobs resume with --address and --expected-public-key for this same job.
   Record reachable/verified and the job's terminal state. Jobs do not pre-enroll:
   require an honestly unenrolled state rather than claiming Cloud success here.
   With owner approval perform one normal reboot, without reflashing or reapplying
   the seed. Within @SECONDS@ seconds repeat steps7–9 with a new boot ID. Require
   the same name, persisted Wi-Fi UUID, Agent hash, identity and actual association.

Case B: configure Wi-Fi while fresh pre-enrollment is waiting (2805)

10. This is a separate fresh-install case, with a second exact-target authorization.
    A previously enrolled board cannot establish the bug. Preserve CaseA evidence,
    restore only through the reserved recovery method, and run the generated
    pre_enroll_fresh_install in a real terminal. It pins --binary, sets --no-wifi
    and reserves the intended Cloud enrollment. Confirm the returned tenant/device
    identity and staged credential provenance privately. Do not print the credential.
    Keep the lab SSID disabled and wired management without Internet. Stop if this
    installer/image does not stage /config/acme-enrollment.json or if a legacy
    handoff also exists. Do not manually fabricate an EAB or delete an attempt marker.

11. Observe the first boot from serial. Within @SECONDS@ seconds require the exact
    pinned Agent to be running and setup RPCs reachable through the direct link.
    Record the actual WENDY_CONFIG_PATH from the unit if overridden; the snapshot
    defaults to /etc/wendy-agent and must use that observed path otherwise.
    Capture the journal's 'Waiting for network connectivity before first-boot
    enrollment' and at least one actual failed public-directory probe. Confirm the
    configured public directory is unreachable over every board egress route.
    Clock/TLS/invalid-directory errors must be classified honestly, not called Wi-Fi
    failure. Require acme-enrollment.json retained, no acme-first-boot-attempt.json,
    no newly issued identity and no automatic credential redemption. Record file
    existence/permissions only, never contents. Observe for 30 seconds after the
    failed probe. RPC status must remain responsive and report unenrolled.

12. Enable only the reserved SSID, timestamp the AP event and run wifi_setup from
    the direct operator endpoint. This case deliberately opts into the documented
    unverified Wi-Fi setup exception for this physically identified unenrolled
    board. Decline host-keychain lookup and type the lab password at the hidden
    terminal prompt. Do not reuse this exception for an enrolled or identity-bound
    device. Do not start a separate enrollment command or restart the Agent to
    assist recovery. Bound the Wi-Fi command to 90 seconds of observation; if it
    stalls interrupt once, retain logs and inspect the same board before recovery.
    Require the intended SSID/BSSID, actual NetworkManager activation, AP station
    event and interface-bound connectivity, as in step8. The unchanged Agent process
    must move from waiting to issuance after connectivity becomes available.

13. Within 180 seconds of Wi-Fi becoming usable, require the journal's directory
    reachable/first-boot completed events, exactly one issuance attempt, durable
    marker/state, and removal of the consumed handoff. Verify expected tenant/device
    principal using local persisted public identity plus install verify with
    --require-enrollment. Record fresh Cloud presence for that exact identity as a
    separate check; reservation alone is not connection evidence. Compare with the
    tenant's issuance/audit record to establish one credential redemption. If that
    record is unavailable, leave the exact issuance-count assertion pending.
    The verify public key before and after enrollment need not be identical: direct
    ACME generates its enrolled key. Record the transition and pin the authenticated
    post-enrollment key for subsequent checks. Do not treat a planned key change as
    an unrelated device, or accept an unexplained principal change.

14. Reboot the same board normally once, with Wi-Fi available and no reinstall or
    enrollment RPC. Within @SECONDS@ seconds require the same enrolled principal,
    post-enrollment public key, Agent hash, persistent hostname/profile and a fresh
    AP association. Require no second account/order issuance and no renewed staged
    credential. A failed/uncertain issuance preserves its marker and needs explicit
    coordinated recovery; never delete the marker to manufacture automatic retry.
    Keep the portable real-ACME fixture evidence separate from this physical result.

Evidence, limits and recovery

15. Preserve each attempt in a fresh private directory: exact source/binary/archive
    hashes, immutable descriptor/plan, target fingerprint and authorization record,
    redacted seed/job records, serial and Agent/NM journals with boot IDs/UTC,
    before/after profile UUID and name, AP/DHCP records, interface-bound packets,
    verification JSON, issuance audit and cleanup result. Export only the measured
    journal interval for the observed service. Record first failure, every timeout
    and any manual action; neither later success nor synthetic state overwrites it.
    An independent reviewer must tie all observations to the same physical target.
    Missing first-boot capture, unverified binary, alternative Internet route or
    unavailable identity evidence leaves the relevant case incomplete.

16. Restore only this reserved board/AP/test Cloud registration using the reviewed
    recovery record. Do not wipe other profiles, tenant devices, host CLI state or
    shared caches. Remove private input/evidence credentials under owner policy only
    after recovery is confirmed; keep sanitized hashes and outcome. This procedure
    covers the executed developer-kit/storage path only. A media-only install,
    another carrier/storage/radio, and WPA3-specific driver acceptance require their
    own actual run. Use orin-wpa3-rehearsal.py for the full SAE/PMF and mixed-network
    cases instead of claiming them from this first-boot association.
